statements.attributed: provides the equation ε˙=Aσnexp(−Q/RT) for steady-state creep rate and the description of activation energy Q
statements.quote: Dependence of the steady-state creep rate (ε˙) on the applied stress (σ) and temperature (T) can be expressed as: ε˙=Aσnexp(−Q/RT), where A is a constant, Q is the activation energy for creep and R is the gas constant, thus the activation energy for creep (Q) can be further described as: Q=−R(−∂lnε˙/∂T−1) under constant loads.

statements.attributed: reports the creep activation energy of CMSX-2 as 230 kJ/mol
statements.quote: From the linear slope of lnε˙ vs. T−1 curve, the creep activation energy of HESA can be estimated to be 290 kJ/mol, while that of CMSX-2 is 230 kJ/mol.

statements.attributed: relates the rafting of γ′ to the positive lattice misfit (δ) between γ and γ′
statements.quote: Therefore, the rafting of γ′ in HESA has shown to coarsen along the direction of the applied stress, which can be related to the positive lattice misfit (δ) between γ and γ′.

statements.attributed: reports that Al10Co25Cr8Fe15Ni36Ti6 contains only 46 vol% of γ′ at room temperature
statements.quote: The tensile strength of HESA can be attributed to the high volume fraction of strengthening precipitates γ′, while previous HEAs like Al10Co25Cr8Fe15Ni36Ti6 contains only 46 vol% of γ′ at room temperature.

statements.attributed: provides strong-pair and weak-pair coupling theories and equations for critical resolved shear stress (τc)
statements.quote: According to strong-pair and weak-pair coupling theories,, the critical resolved shear stress (τc) of the precipitation strengthened alloys can be determined by the factors of APB energy, volume fraction of γ′ and γ′ size as: τc=γAPB2b[(6γAPBfrπT)1/2−f] and τc=32(Gbr)f1/2wπ3/2(2πγAPBrwGb2−1)1/2, where γ APB is the APB energy, f is the volume fraction of γ′, r is the γ′ radius, T is the line tension, G is the shear modulus, b is the Burgers vector and w is a dimensionless constant.

statements.attributed: indicates that peak strength is yielded when the γ′ radius (r) increases to around 2TγAPB
statements.quote: Since these theories have indicated that the peak strength would be yielded as the r increases to around 2TγAPB , and with the similar volume fraction of γ′ between HESA (69 vol%) and CMSX-2 (68 vol%), the optimized size of γ′ for peak strength in HESA can be estimated from that of CMSX-2.

statements.attributed: reports that tensile strength of CMSX-2 is significantly improved with an increase in average γ′ size from 300 nm to 450 nm
statements.quote: In addition, due to the tensile strength of CMSX-2 has been reported to be significantly improved with an increase in average γ′ size from 300 nm to 450 nm, and with the inversely proportional relationship to APB energy, the optimized size of γ′ in HESA should be around 390 nm; however, the as heat-treated γ′ size is only 290 nm in this work.

statements.attributed: describes the correlation between SFE, creep activation energy, and creep strain rate with the equation ε˙=A′(γSF/Gb)3(σ/G)5exp(−Q/RT)
statements.quote: The correlation between SFE, creep activation energy and creep strain rate is described as: ε˙=A′(γSF/Gb)3(σ/G)5exp(−Q/RT), where A′ is a constant, γSF is the stacking fault energy, G is the shear modulus, b is the Burgers vector, Q is the activation energy of creep and σ is the applied stress, so the lower SFE and higher Q of HESA can lead to lower creep rates.
